name: Malluch
overview: Malluch was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, identified in the book of Nehemiah. He is notably mentioned as one of the signatories on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, specifically in Nehemiah 10:4. His priestly role highlights his significance in the religious restoration efforts during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Malluch, as found in Nehemiah 10:4, means 'counselor' or 'king,' reflecting a title of honor or leadership. A variant of his name, Malluchi, appears in Nehemiah 12:14 with the same meaning. These names emphasize a role associated with guidance or authority within the community.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jonathan as Malluch's father, inferred from Nehemiah 12:14. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text for Malluch.
scriptureSignificance: Malluch's importance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest who participated in the solemn covenant renewal among the returned exiles. By affixing his seal to the document in Nehemiah 10, he demonstrated commitment to the law of God and the communal reforms under Nehemiah's leadership. His presence underscores the active involvement of the priesthood in reestablishing covenant faithfulness during Israel's restoration.
